ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, vertex $C$ of $ABCD$ is on the side $BF$ of the equilateral triangle $\triangle BEF$, with point $E$ on the extension of $AB$, and $G$ as the midpoint of $DE$. Connecting $CG$. If $AD=5$, $AB=CF=3$, then what is the length of $CG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: As shown in the figure, extend DC to meet EF at point H, \\
$\because$ $\square ABCD$, AD=5, AB=CF=3, \\
$\therefore$ AD$\parallel$BC, BC=5, CD=CF=3, \\
$\therefore$ BF=BC+CF=5+3=8, $\angle$FCH=$\angle$EBF, \\
$\because$ equilateral $\triangle BEF$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle F=\angle BEF=\angle EBF=\angle FCH=60^\circ$, EF=BF=8, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle FCH$ is an equilateral triangle, \\
$\therefore$ CH=CF=FH=3, \\
$\therefore$ HE=EF−HF=8−3=5, \\
also $\because$ G is the midpoint of DE, \\
$\therefore$ CG is the midline of $\triangle DHE$, \\
$\therefore$ CG=$\frac{1}{2}$HE=$\frac{1}{2} \times 5=\boxed{\frac{5}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the base points A, B, E are approximately on the same straight line, and E is on the extension of AB to the right; B, F, E form an equilateral triangle, and C is located on side BF. Quadrilateral ABCD is drawn in the shape of a parallelogram, with AB parallel to CD and AD parallel to BC. Segment DE has been drawn, point G is on DE, and CG has been connected. Reasoning: According to the auxiliary-line method, extend DC to intersect EF at H. Because ABCD is a parallelogram, and AD=5, AB=3, therefore BC=AD=5, CD=AB=3. It is also known that CF=3, and C is on BF, therefore BF=BC+CF=5+3=8. Since triangle BEF is an equilateral triangle, EF=BF=8, and each angle is 60°. Also because DC is parallel to AB, and AB and BE are collinear, therefore CH is parallel to BE; therefore ∠FCH equals ∠FBE in the equilateral triangle, which is 60°. At the same time, FH is on EF, FC is on FB, and ∠CFH is also 60°, so triangle FCH is an equilateral triangle. Thus FH=CF=CH=3. Hence HE=EF-FH=8-3=5. Since C is on DH, and G is the midpoint of DE, therefore in triangle DHE, CG is a midline, so CG=HE/2=5/2.
